Subject Local National Salvation Elements promote "Thrift Society".
Made by D.S. McKeown    Forwarded by [Signature]

Instructions are respectfully requested for the disposal
of the remaining two prisoners now in custody at the Chengtu
Road Station connected with the promotion of a "Thrift "
movement as a cloak to further the anti-Japanese boycott
movement.

The following is a summary of the evidence against these
two persons:-

(1) Chiang Wen-kwei (蒋文桂), one of the leaders of the
movement, admits being assigned by the Communist Party
to investigate and report the labour situation in the
Commercial Press. A preparatory member of the Communist
Party. Secret communist publication entitled "Truth
(真言 )" found in his home. "Knowledge for new party
members," and 27 other kinds of anti-Japanese and leftist
literature. One of the publishers of the magazine entitled
"Long Hwa (Wave)", a secret publication previously unknown,
containing national salvation propaganda. Responsible
for distribution of the magazine "Unity" among the workers
of the Commercial Press. Also served as purchasing agent
for anti-Japanese and Communist books published in Hankow.

(2) Soong Hsi-vung(宋希文): A member of the "Thrift Society"
Attended two secret meetings. Arranged for the printing
of 60 copies of a handbill bearing on the "Thrift move-
ment," national salvation in nature. Implicated by Tsang
Hei-ngoch as a promoter of the "After Office Hours
Reading Society," which according to Chiang Wen Kwei was
to promote the National Salvation movement. Introduced
one member to the "Thrift Society."

（左侧批注：D.S. McKeown 17/8）

TRANSLATION OF A PETITION SUBMITTED BY WONG KYING-
FOH (王金福), BROTHER OF WONG KYING-DAO (王景陶)
( IN CUSTODY ). WONG KYING-FOH IS A NATIVE OF
SHANGHAI, FORMERLY RESIDING AT 11 WONG KA ZAH,
WEST PAOSHENG ROAD, CHAPEI, AND AT PRESENT LIVING
AT NO. 345 HUH DAH LI, RUE BOURGEAT.

I beg to state that Wong Kying-dao (王景陶),
a iae King Dau (金桃), is my younger brother, age 21.
After graduating from the Footung Primary School (浦东小学),
he attended the Ming Jang Middle School, North Paoshing
Road, Chapei, and completed his course in the junior mid-
dle school in 1935. During his study in that school, he
was a favourite student of his school-master Dr. R.J. Bryan
who has returned to the U.S.A. He is very diligent and
honest, and is a member of the Baptist Church. He continued
to study in the Ming Jang School until the outbreak of the
August 13th incident, when the institute closed. The master
was then Mr. James Hamilton Ware.

My brother then joined the Chien Chwang Middle
School, 318 Weihaiwei Road in order to complete his middle
school course. He graduated this summer, and decided to
receive an advanced course. Owing to financial difficulties,
he, on the information of his school-mates, and being a
Christian, applied to the Church Office at Yuen Ming Yuen
Road, for monetary assistance. His request was approved
with the recommendation of the principal of the Ming Jang
Middle School certifying that he is of good behavior and
excellent education. Consequently he started to refresh
his mind of his old lessons and used to apply to the
teachers of the Chien Chwang Middle School for assistance
in solving difficult problems.

On July 24 (Sunday), at about 8 a.m., my brother
left for the Chien Chwang School, carrying with him a
physics book, with the intention of asking his teacher to
explain some problems relating to physics. The teacher
was absent, so my brother remained on the premises and

- 2 -
read newspapers to await the return of the physics teacher.
At about 9.30 a.m., he was arrested in a class
room without any reason to his knowledge. (The above
information was obtained from a servant of the Chien
Chwang Middle School.)
My brother was not acquainted with any persons
who attended during the meeting, and I believe that this
point has been brought to your notice. He has never joined
any public bodies or participated in the formation of any
organizations. He was seldom out except going to school
(this can be proved by our neighbours). He is quite a good
person and it appears to be a mistake to arrest him.
Subsequent to his arrest, my mother has been
very uneasy. She partakes of only a little food, and is
nearly in a state of mental disorder. She simply hopes for
the return of her son.
I herewith submitted a petition together with
a letter of Mr. James Hamilton Ware, principal of the Ming
Jang Middle School to certify that Wong Kying-foh is a
peaceful man and beg you to release him forthwith.

(chopped) Wong Kying-foh.
August 2, 1938.

Ta Kei Pao and other local newspapers :- 9 AUG. 1938 A.M.

LOCAL THRIFT MOVEMENT

As a response to the thrift movement promoted by the National Government, leaders of various local Chinese circles are starting a thrift movement. On August 8, they issued the following circular addressed to Chinese residents in this locality :-
"Since the commencement of the war of resistance of China, the Chinese people have been closely consolidated and been struggling with an undaunted spirit for a final victory. We, living in this isolated island, are suffering from the increased cost of living and a large number of refugees are sheltered in the Foreign Settlements in the most distressful condition. It is true that various local amusement resorts are doing business far better than before and that dance halls, theatres, tea rooms and cabarets are always overcrowded. This shows that people in this isolated island are lovers of luxury, giving no consideration to national affairs.
"Japan, the invading race, is exercising thrift. Can we, the invaded people, whose houses have been gutted or whose families have been lost, waste our money lavishly for meaningless amusement? Local Chinese residents should immediately exercise thrift in their clothing and food. The money thus saved should be contributed towards the fund for the relief of refugees."
